title: Human purpose of economy
statement: The economy exists to serve human flourishing, not to make people serve wealth.
text: The economy exists to serve human flourishing, not to make people serve wealth.
explanation: Economic institutions are judged by whether they expand the conditions for people, families, and communities to live purposeful lives.
prohibits: treating growth as the sole end
open_questions: Which measures of flourishing should guide public assessment?

title: Constitutional accountability
statement: Economic power must be accountable to constitutional rules and democratic institutions.
text: Economic power must be accountable to constitutional rules and democratic institutions.
explanation: Private authority can shape civic life as profoundly as public authority, so both require lawful limits and remedies.
implications: apply due process to economic regulation
open_questions: What constitutional tests apply to private power?

title: Private property
statement: Secure private property is a foundation of liberty, responsibility, and independence.
text: Secure private property is a foundation of liberty, responsibility, and independence.
explanation: Ownership gives people durable standing to plan, create, exchange, and resist arbitrary control.
open_questions: How should public obligations of property be defined?

title: Free enterprise
statement: People should be free to start, improve, and exchange through lawful enterprise.
text: People should be free to start, improve, and exchange through lawful enterprise.
explanation: Open entry and voluntary exchange create opportunity when rules prevent coercion, fraud, and exclusion.
implications: protect freedom of contract within fair rules
open_questions: Which regulations protect rather than burden free enterprise?

title: Limited and capable government
statement: Government must be limited by law and capable of enforcing the common rules of a free economy.
text: Government must be limited by law and capable of enforcing the common rules of a free economy.
explanation: Weak government invites private domination; unlimited government threatens liberty. Constitutional capacity is neither absence nor control of government.
open_questions: What capacities are essential at each level of government?

title: Broad ownership
statement: A free society should widen meaningful access to ownership of homes, savings, businesses, and productive assets.
text: A free society should widen meaningful access to ownership of homes, savings, businesses, and productive assets.
explanation: Dispersed ownership strengthens independence and makes prosperity more durable and broadly shared.
open_questions: Which ownership pathways are most scalable?

title: Dignity of work
statement: Work deserves respect, fair terms, and a real path to security and advancement.
text: Work deserves respect, fair terms, and a real path to security and advancement.
explanation: Workers are citizens and contributors, not merely variable costs.
open_questions: Which labor standards best preserve flexibility and dignity?

title: Responsible ownership
statement: Ownership carries responsibilities to use power lawfully and avoid foreseeable harm to others.
text: Ownership carries responsibilities to use power lawfully and avoid foreseeable harm to others.
explanation: Property rights are strengthened, not negated, when owners remain answerable for the effects of their conduct.
open_questions: Where should responsibility end and public regulation begin?

title: Fair competition
statement: Markets should reward better service and innovation under rules that keep rivalry real.
text: Markets should reward better service and innovation under rules that keep rivalry real.
explanation: Competition is a constitutional condition of economic liberty, not a guarantee that every firm succeeds.
open_questions: How should competition law account for digital platforms?

title: Anti-concentration
statement: No private institution should accumulate economic power sufficient to dominate markets, communities, or politics.
text: No private institution should accumulate economic power sufficient to dominate markets, communities, or politics.
explanation: Concentration can turn nominal markets and elections into systems of dependency.
open_questions: What thresholds signal domination rather than scale?

title: Local economic resilience
statement: Economic policy should preserve the capacity of communities to sustain livelihoods and adapt to shocks.
text: Economic policy should preserve the capacity of communities to sustain livelihoods and adapt to shocks.
explanation: Resilient local institutions reduce dependence on distant, unaccountable decision makers.
open_questions: How can local resilience avoid protectionism?

title: Transparent taxation
statement: Taxes should be lawful, understandable, fairly administered, and visible to those who bear them.
text: Taxes should be lawful, understandable, fairly administered, and visible to those who bear them.
explanation: A constitutional tax system lets citizens evaluate obligations and prevents hidden transfers of power.
open_questions: How should destination-based taxation be designed?

title: Market-access responsibility
statement: Access to markets created and protected by law carries duties not to exploit that public framework.
text: Access to markets created and protected by law carries duties not to exploit that public framework.
explanation: Corporate privileges, infrastructure, and enforceable contracts are public conditions that justify reciprocal responsibility.
open_questions: Which duties should be legal versus voluntary?

title: Intergenerational stewardship
statement: Economic choices should preserve opportunity, institutions, and natural resources for those who follow.
text: Economic choices should preserve opportunity, institutions, and natural resources for those who follow.
explanation: Present consumption must not impose avoidable, unaccountable burdens on future citizens.
prohibits: shifting avoidable costs to future generations
open_questions: What representation can future citizens receive?

title: Technological shared prosperity
statement: Technology should expand broadly shared capability and opportunity, not merely concentrate returns and control.
text: Technology should expand broadly shared capability and opportunity, not merely concentrate returns and control.
explanation: Innovation is welcome, while its institutional gains and disruptions require accountable governance.
open_questions: What obligations accompany AI-driven displacement?

title: Due process
statement: Economic rules and enforcement must provide notice, neutral procedures, and meaningful appeal.
text: Economic rules and enforcement must provide notice, neutral procedures, and meaningful appeal.
explanation: Neither public agencies nor powerful private systems should impose opaque, unreviewable deprivation.
open_questions: How does due process apply to platforms?

title: Reform without revolution
statement: Needed economic reform should proceed through lawful, peaceful, and institution-building means.
text: Needed economic reform should proceed through lawful, peaceful, and institution-building means.
explanation: A constitutional project seeks correction of injustice without discarding liberty, continuity, or democratic legitimacy.
open_questions: When are transition measures sufficiently protective?

title: International adaptability
statement: Constitutional Capitalism offers principles for adaptation, not a single nation’s policy template.
text: Constitutional Capitalism offers principles for adaptation, not a single nation’s policy template.
explanation: Different legal traditions and development levels require locally legitimate institutional expressions.
open_questions: Which principles are universal and which context-bound?

title: Democratic accountability
statement: Economic policy must remain answerable to citizens through representative, transparent, and lawful institutions.
text: Economic policy must remain answerable to citizens through representative, transparent, and lawful institutions.
explanation: Democracy requires citizens to be able to understand, contest, and change economic rules.
open_questions: How can accountability be protected from moneyed influence?

title: Separation of economic and political domination
statement: A free republic must prevent either wealth from buying governing power or government from arbitrarily commanding private life.
text: A free republic must prevent either wealth from buying governing power or government from arbitrarily commanding private life.
explanation: The separation is a reciprocal safeguard: economic liberty needs political equality, and political liberty needs independent civil society.
open_questions: What institutional safeguards best enforce this separation?

title: Distributed constitutional power
statement: Power should be distributed as close as possible to the people who create and sustain society.
text: Power should be distributed as close as possible to the people who create and sustain society.
explanation: Constitutional Capitalism organizes around where power should reside in a republic, not around expanding government, corporate, or factional control as ends in themselves.
implications: apply subsidiarity intuition to ownership and economic benefit
open_questions: Which functions demonstrably require national scale?

title: Subsidiarity extended to ownership
statement: Authority, ownership, and economic benefit should remain as close as reasonably possible to the people and communities that create the value, unless a broader level of organization is demonstrably necessary.
text: Authority, ownership, and economic benefit should remain as close as reasonably possible to the people and communities that create the value, unless a broader level of organization is demonstrably necessary.
explanation: The philosophy shares the classical intuition of subsidiarity and extends it into economics, ownership, and constitutional accountability rather than claiming a brand-new discovery.
implications: map the power hierarchy before proposing national fixes
open_questions: How is necessity at a higher level demonstrated?

title: People as source of national capacity
statement: The people are the nation's greatest source of productive capacity, creativity, innovation, and self-government.
text: The people are the nation's greatest source of productive capacity, creativity, innovation, and self-government.
explanation: Investing in health, education, security, and opportunity can be productive investment. People remain citizens with dignity — never merely inputs or resources to be used.
implications: evaluate systems by human flourishing and capacity
open_questions: Which human-capacity investments show strongest evidence?

title: Stewardship across generations
statement: Each generation must improve and pass on the constitutional, economic, and social inheritance it receives.
text: Each generation must improve and pass on the constitutional, economic, and social inheritance it receives.
explanation: Stewardship gives the philosophy a long horizon: land, institutions, infrastructure, knowledge, public trust, and constitutional government are held in trust for those who follow.
open_questions: How should stewardship metrics enter the National Baseline?

title: Duty of constructive improvement
statement: No generation inherits a perfect system; every generation has a duty to improve it for the next through evidence, reason, and constitutional process.
text: No generation inherits a perfect system; every generation has a duty to improve it for the next through evidence, reason, and constitutional process.
explanation: Improving the philosophy and the system for all is among the highest forms of civic service. Blind loyalty and mere destruction both fail this duty.
implications: make Living Amendments a first-class project surface
open_questions: What process governs philosophical amendments?

title: Community economic sovereignty
statement: Communities should retain enough productive and institutional capacity to remain resilient and prosperous without permanent dependence on distant centers.
text: Communities should retain enough productive and institutional capacity to remain resilient and prosperous without permanent dependence on distant centers.
explanation: This is economic sovereignty, not a claim of political secession. It asks whether communities can feed, educate, care, finance, house, and train locally — and why not if they cannot.
implications: measure community capabilities in the National Baseline
open_questions: Which resilience capacities are minimum viable?

title: Corporations as constitutional partners
statement: Corporations that benefit from a community share responsibility for sustaining the conditions that allow that community to flourish.
text: Corporations that benefit from a community share responsibility for sustaining the conditions that allow that community to flourish.
explanation: A corporation's primary function is efficient, sustainable production of goods and services. Broader social goods are shared responsibilities. Corporations are partners — not governments and not rulers.
implications: frame corporate duties as partnership, not total social welfare assignment
open_questions: Which reciprocal duties are enforceable vs cultural?

title: Essential infrastructure accessibility
statement: Essential infrastructure that enables participation in modern economic life should be broadly accessible.
text: Essential infrastructure that enables participation in modern economic life should be broadly accessible.
explanation: Transportation, broadband, and similar arteries may become so fundamental that exclusion blocks opportunity. Institutional form — public, private, cooperative, or hybrid — remains a design question under the principle.
prohibits: treating essential access as optional luxury without analysis
implications: separate principle from ownership model debates
open_questions: Which infrastructures meet the essentiality threshold where?

title: Equal standing before the Constitution
statement: Every person stands equal before the Constitution. Neither wealth, office, race, religion, political affiliation, social status, birthplace, celebrity, nor institutional influence shall increase or diminish the protection of the law or the accountability imposed by the law.
text: Every person stands equal before the Constitution. Neither wealth, office, race, religion, political affiliation, social status, birthplace, celebrity, nor institutional influence shall increase or diminish the protection of the law or the accountability imposed by the law.
explanation: Foundational constitutional principle of equal protection and equal accountability. Equal standing is not identical treatment of every situation: the law may legitimately distinguish a child from an adult, or a person convicted after due process from one who has not been convicted. Status must not determine justice. Complements Declaration 'On equality,' which rejects equality of outcome. Blind Stage Principle: evaluate conduct before identity whenever constitutionally and practically possible. Iconic guide: The Constitution should hear the evidence before it sees the person.
prohibits: special treatment by wealth or influence
equality of outcome as a constitutional mandate
implications: Equal Standing Test for proposed laws
equal access architecture (representation, understandable law, records, appeals)
shared civic identity under a common constitutional standard
open_questions: Which access-to-justice minimums are constitutionally required vs policy design?
How should role-specific duties (licensed professions, officeholders) be framed without creating privileged castes?

title: Self-government requires civic preparation
statement: Self-government requires education. A constitutional republic has a duty to prepare every generation to understand its rights, its responsibilities, its institutions, and its ability to improve society through peaceful civic participation.
text: Self-government requires education. A constitutional republic has a duty to prepare every generation to understand its rights, its responsibilities, its institutions, and its ability to improve society through peaceful civic participation.
explanation: Core Constitutional Citizenship Doctrine. Democracy is a skill, not merely a right. The primary question is how to graduate every citizen prepared for responsible self-government — not merely at what age someone may vote. Citizenship is learned through experience: continuous civic education, practical service, and meaningful contribution to community decision-making. Complements Human Capital and Equal Standing. Earlier local voting ideas are pilot candidates under certified preparation — not a locked age rule.
prohibits: assuming automatic readiness at a birthday
symbolic youth councils with no real advisory role
locking national voting-age expansion without evidence
implications: pilot-and-measure posture for earlier local participation
open_questions: Which civic competencies are minimum for graduation vs enrichment?
Under what measured conditions could earlier local participation strengthen representation?

title: Encourage participation, not ideology
statement: Government should encourage participation, not ideology. Public education may recognize civic participation regardless of viewpoint, but may not require students to support or oppose any candidate, party, or policy position as a condition of graduation.
text: Government should encourage participation, not ideology. Public education may recognize civic participation regardless of viewpoint, but may not require students to support or oppose any candidate, party, or policy position as a condition of graduation.
explanation: Preserves public trust and constitutional neutrality in civic education. Students are rewarded for respectful participation, constitutional understanding, evidence evaluation, community engagement, and constructive contribution — never for agreeing with government, a party, or teachers. Campaign or advocacy work may count only under equal, viewpoint-neutral standards alongside nonpartisan alternatives. Complements Constitutional Citizenship (CC-PRIN-30) and Equal Standing.
protects: equal recognition of lawful civic pathways
prohibits: graduation credit that requires partisan agreement
favoring one political viewpoint in school civic-credit programs
implications: Civic Service Portfolio with optional safeguarded political participation
Civic Achievement Transcript as experience record, not conformity score
reflection focused on democratic practice, not predetermined conclusions
open_questions: What audit and complaint processes best enforce viewpoint-neutral credit recognition?
How should schools document equal standards when optional campaign work is recognized?

title: Children and family-first republic
statement: A nation's greatest long-term asset is not its money, its corporations, or its natural resources. It is the children it raises. Strong families create strong communities; strong communities create a strong republic; public institutions should strengthen families rather than replace them whenever possible.
text: A nation's greatest long-term asset is not its money, its corporations, or its natural resources. It is the children it raises. Strong families create strong communities; strong communities create a strong republic; public institutions should strengthen families rather than replace them whenever possible.
explanation: Major Constitutional Family Doctrine pillar. Children are the shared responsibility of families, communities, and ultimately the republic until prepared to become healthy, capable, independent participants — not until they are 'productive,' a phrasing rejected because worth must not depend on economic output. Parents remain primary caregivers. Care climbs a subsidiarity ladder. No child should lack adequate nutrition because of circumstances beyond the child's control, with the state as guarantor of last resort. Intergenerational prosperity removes barriers to voluntary family connection. Child flourishing asks whether children are better prepared than the generation before them.
protects: human-capital investment in the next generation
prohibits: treating children's worth as economic output
state-first replacement of families whenever avoidable
abandoning children when local support fails
implications: links to Human Capital, Food Security, Citizenship, Equal Standing
open_questions: Which child-flourishing indicators are first-sourced in Phase 2.1?
How should inheritance and multigenerational housing reforms be piloted without locking national design?

title: Human flourishing as defining benchmark
statement: The measure of Constitutional Capitalism is whether human life improved. Every major proposal should answer whether it measurably increases human flourishing for people, families, and communities — not GDP, markets, spending, or profits alone.
text: The measure of Constitutional Capitalism is whether human life improved. Every major proposal should answer whether it measurably increases human flourishing for people, families, and communities — not GDP, markets, spending, or profits alone.
explanation: Human Flourishing Index is the defining benchmark architecture. Domains include health, family stability, childhood well-being, education, civic participation, ownership, resilience, environment, trust, safety, opportunity, time with family, volunteerism, culture, and life satisfaction. Architecture is not measurement; indicator values remain pending until sourced. Modeling remains 0%.
implications: policy test question on every major proposal
Systems Map and Knowledge Graph as organizing tools
open_questions: Which HFI domains are sourced first without false precision?
How should weights be deferred until a meaningful sourced subset exists?

title: Assistance as security, capacity, and independence
statement: No person should be abandoned when unable to meet essential needs. No institution should trap a capable person in dependency. Assistance should protect dignity, strengthen capacity, reward productive advancement, and lead toward the greatest independence reasonably possible — guaranteeing security while dismantling dependency.
text: No person should be abandoned when unable to meet essential needs. No institution should trap a capable person in dependency. Assistance should protect dignity, strengthen capacity, reward productive advancement, and lead toward the greatest independence reasonably possible — guaranteeing security while dismantling dependency.
explanation: Major Assistance Doctrine pillar. Rejects one-size-fits-all assistance. Distinguishes security (hunger, illness, disability, childhood, caregiving, or temporary job loss will not destroy life) from dependency (rules that punish work, marriage, saving, promotion, entrepreneurship, or property). Six pathways; gradual phaseouts so every additional hour of productive work leaves households better off; Human Prosperity Account and Prosperity Navigators; foundations of participation before requirements; Community Work Guarantee as alternative to UBI; employer responsibility; asset-building; fair reciprocity; fraud without humiliation; exit measurement by capability and connection. Exact phaseout rates require modeling (0%).
protects: people unable to meet essential needs
pathway to income, ownership, and participation
prohibits: treating all recipients as the same problem
managing a dependent population as the objective
implications: links Family, Food Security, Human Capital, Public Service, Equal Standing, HFI
open_questions: What gradual phaseout schedules survive modeling without recreating cliffs across stacked programs?
How should Pathway F reciprocity be piloted with due-process safeguards?
What Community Work Guarantee pilots avoid displacement and stigma?

title: Limited, capable, transparent, and focused federal government
statement: The federal government exists to protect constitutional liberty, defend the nation, preserve a fair national system, coordinate what communities and states cannot accomplish alone, and restrain powers that exceed local control. All other authority should remain as close to the people as competence and constitutional rights permit. Power remains local unless its exercise requires national coordination, national uniformity, or protection of constitutional rights.
text: The federal government exists to protect constitutional liberty, defend the nation, preserve a fair national system, coordinate what communities and states cannot accomplish alone, and restrain powers that exceed local control. All other authority should remain as close to the people as competence and constitutional rights permit. Power remains local unless its exercise requires national coordination, national uniformity, or protection of constitutional rights.
explanation: Major Federalism Doctrine pillar. Rejects defining the federal government as weak. Defines it as limited, capable, transparent, and focused. Core responsibilities include constitutional rights floors, defense and foreign affairs, currency and fiscal stability with People’s Ledger transparency, interstate commerce, competition and concentrated-power restraint, national infrastructure standards, public-data infrastructure, baseline national protections, temporary emergency coordination, and regional redistribution that strengthens local capacity. Federal grants must not become domination. Agencies face periodic renew/consolidate/transfer/end review. Legal drafting of statutes remains 0%.
protects: republic against concentrated private and political power
transparent federal fiscal and administrative power
prohibits: treating the federal government as weak by design
routine federal management of ordinary local life
permanent emergency expansions of federal control
grant conditions that dictate identical local delivery models without necessity
agencies without measurable outcomes or sunset review
using funding to bypass constitutional limits
implications: links Equal Standing, Transparency, Democracy, Capacity, Assistance, Family, RCIP
open_questions: Which existing federal agencies fail the periodic review questions under this doctrine?
How should People’s Ledger real-time disclosure be specified without inventing systems that do not yet exist?
What grant-redesign pilots preserve floors while maximizing local delivery flexibility?

title: Popular sovereignty and the People’s Branch
statement: All governmental authority originates in the people and remains held in trust for them. Elections do not surrender that authority for the duration of a term. The people retain peaceful, structured, and constitutionally protected powers to propose laws, reject laws, recall officials, audit institutions, amend constitutions, and reform every branch of government — while remaining bound by the same fundamental rights floor as every other branch.
text: All governmental authority originates in the people and remains held in trust for them. Elections do not surrender that authority for the duration of a term. The people retain peaceful, structured, and constitutionally protected powers to propose laws, reject laws, recall officials, audit institutions, amend constitutions, and reform every branch of government — while remaining bound by the same fundamental rights floor as every other branch.
explanation: Major Popular Sovereignty Doctrine. Constitutes the Sovereign People as a fourth branch and first source of authority. Reserved powers include initiative, referendum, citizen veto, carefully safeguarded recall, People’s Amendment Process, limited conventions, and citizen audits. Courts remain independent enough to protect rights and accountable enough that corruption and abuse cannot hide behind independence. Ordinary partisan recall of Supreme Court justices is rejected. Federal redesign requires constitutional amendment. Legal drafting remains 0%.
protects: judicial independence to protect unpopular persons
accountability for judicial ethics and abuse of office
deliberative rather than purely advertising-driven ballots
prohibits: treating elections as a full surrender of sovereignty for a term
ordinary partisan recall of Supreme Court justices
ballot measures that strip equal protection, due process, or dignity
wealth capture of petition and ballot campaigns
unexplained nationally consequential emergency judicial orders as a substitute for adjudication
implications: links Federalism, Equal Standing, Democracy, Transparency, Citizenship
open_questions: Which illustrative signature and ratification thresholds survive turnout and capture modeling?
How should a Judicial Accountability Council be appointed without recreating partisan capture?
What limited-convention safeguards are sufficient against runaway agendas?

title: Public office confers responsibility, not privilege
statement: Public office confers responsibility, not privilege. Elected officials shall remain participants in the same civic systems they establish for the people. No office shall create a permanent political class or guarantee lifelong benefits unavailable to similarly situated citizens. The highest reward for faithful public service is the continued trust and respect of a free people, not permanent governmental privilege.
text: Public office confers responsibility, not privilege. Elected officials shall remain participants in the same civic systems they establish for the people. No office shall create a permanent political class or guarantee lifelong benefits unavailable to similarly situated citizens. The highest reward for faithful public service is the continued trust and respect of a free people, not permanent governmental privilege.
explanation: Major complementary Public Service Doctrine. Eliminates special privileges tied to holding office while preserving benefits earned under the same contribution and eligibility rules as everyone else. Officials should live under the systems they create. Public office is not a career plan for permanent governmental employment. Supports a citizen legislature, fair transparent compensation, carefully tailored cooling-off rules, radical transparency, and civic honor rather than lifelong privilege. Complements the existing public-service modernization spine. Architecture only; no invented benefit-package statistics; legal drafting 0%.
protects: equal civic status of officials and citizens
benefits earned under generally applicable rules
ordinary citizens’ ability to afford to serve
public trust through transparency and cooling-off rules
prohibits: lifetime healthcare solely because someone held office
special retirement formulas unavailable to ordinary citizens
permanent taxpayer-funded privileges tied only to elected office
treating public office as a permanent employment track inside government
implications: links public-service modernization, People’s Branch, Federalism, Equal Standing
open_questions: Which current office-tied benefits are privileges versus generally applicable earned benefits under equal rules?
What cooling-off durations survive constitutional and livelihood-fairness review?
How should independent compensation review be structured to remain nonpartisan?
